analysis.title: Hartnett: "The Most Bullish Thing The Fed Can Do Now Is Hike" (Flow Show: Midterms, Bidterms, Skidterms)
key_insights: Hartnett's new Biggest Picture is 'bonds end bubbles'. Korean bond yields are up 200bps in 18 months and Mirae Asset, Korea's largest retail broker, is down 65% since May after a 4-bagger, even though Korean equities are still +98.9% YTD.
Hartnett lists an October Fed rate hike 'to cap yields' as the most bullish event into year-end, alongside gridlock/Goldilocks midterms and a Spain flip to a center-right government.
Global tightening: 54 central bank rate hikes in 2026, and world central banks are tightening on net for the first time since September 2023.

YTD scoreboard: oil 58.5%, US stocks 13.4%, global stocks 10.6%, US$ 3.9%, cash 2.8%, HY bonds -0.5%, IG -3.2%, govt bonds -4.4%, gold -4.8%, bitcoin -6.7%. Government bonds are 7.2 points behind cash.

Last week the 10Y touched 5.36% and the 30Y hit its highest level since 2002. The 10Y auction priced at the highest yield since 2000 but drew near-record foreign demand and calmed the market. The 30Y priced at 5.618% at Thursday's auction.

BofA rates team says the rise in yields is mostly growth and partly uncertainty, with supply, commodities and fiscal worries as lesser factors. Powell's Jackson Hole guidance (policy restrictive, rates eventually near 3%) versus Warsh being 'hard pressed' to see conditions as restrictive 'cut the anchor line'. Rates keep rising until data or markets say stop, and neither condition is judged satisfied.
BofA US economists show the 10Y yield rise since late September is driven by term premium, not by expected Fed funds path.

September FOMC minutes showed all 19 officials backed the hike, with most seeing another hike by year-end. Williams and Jefferson signaled a slower quarterly pace and Waller's base case is Dec and March. The market prices a 17% chance of a hike on Oct 28 and 81% for Dec 9. BofA rates strategists disagree and are paying Oct FOMC OIS: 'hike or bond spike'.

BofA economist Claudio Irigoyen argues the rate spike exposes unsustainable fiscal policy (time inconsistency). Debt/GDP rose about 50pp in France and 60pp in the US over 20 years, both now around 120% of GDP with primary deficits above 2.5%. US headline deficit is about 6% of GDP vs about 5% for France.

France: OAT-Bund spread is 140bps, the widest since the 2011/12 euro crisis, after the fastest selloff in French sovereign spreads in at least 20 years. BofA's Barnaby Martin cites French private non-financial debt at 214% of GDP vs 140% in the US, and no primary surplus since 1974. French bonds are having their worst decade since 1803.

BofA rates team expects OAT-Bunds to settle in a 100-150bp range. A fast move to the top of the range raises odds of backstops (shorter issuance, ECB jawboning, eventually the TPI). BofA European strategists upgraded French stocks to overweight, saying the Stoxx 600's 5% drop from its August high is almost entirely explained by higher US real yields.

Hikes are not 'biting' yet per BofA's Martin: no rollover in US hard data, global forward EPS estimates or hyperscaler capex expectations. A rollover in US macro data would mark the peak in rates vol and the green light for credit.

BofA HY team ('The problem with credit is rates'): less than 30% of September's HY spread widening is explained by refinancing costs or expected losses, the rest is a rates-vol premium. CCC spreads hit 1,200bps, the highest since 2022.
Hartnett: equity breadth improves as yields peak. 394 stocks are within 10% of 52-week highs and 206 within 20%, despite S&P 500 all-time highs, compared with 1999.

EPFR flows for the week: $166.4bn to cash (biggest since April 2020), $33.8bn to bonds, $12.4bn to stocks, $2.0bn to gold, $0.6bn out of crypto. Treasuries +$16.2bn (biggest since April 2025), IG +$10.3bn, bank loans +$2.4bn (biggest since Feb 2025), tech +$3.5bn, Japan stocks -$3.3bn, financials -$3.0bn.

Money market fund assets are about $8tn, up from $5tn in 2023, generating about $330bn a year of interest income with T-bills at 4.2%. Cash has only been deployed after big easing or sustained cuts: 'no rate cuts, no cash cuts'.

BofA Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 8.1 from 8.8 (9.3 two weeks ago), still in sell territory. Sell signal triggered May 26 and global stocks are up 1.7% since. Global Breadth Rule shows net 50% of global indices oversold, the most since April 2025. The contrarian buy signal triggers at net 88%.

Nov 3 midterms are the likely catalyst for a 10% move either way into 2027. Polymarket gives Democrats a 64% chance of a sweep (up from 49% in September), 28% for GOP Senate/Dem House, 9% GOP sweep. Trump approval is 38%.

Hartnett's midterm scenarios: Dem sweep = risk-off, stocks down more than 10%, dollar and yields fall; GOP Senate/Dem House = risk-on, stocks up more than 5% ('Gridlock = Goldilocks'); GOP sweep = stocks up more than 10%. The outcome the market thinks most likely is the one Hartnett sees as most bearish.

Latin America political shift: Bolsonaro won Brazil's first round (runoff Oct 25). Brazilian stocks hit all-time highs and 10-year yields fell a record 124bps in a day. MSCI LatAm is still 35% below its all-time high and Hartnett calls it the best trade to play the US 'Monroe Doctrine'.
Spain's Sánchez called a snap election for Nov 29 with the center-right leading in polls, which Hartnett calls an underrated positive for Euro bonds.

Hartnett leans risk-off into the midterms because of central bank tightening, tighter financial conditions and credit 'canaries' (AUD/JPY, risk parity, Oracle and SoftBank CDS). He would not add to tech since investors are max long, thinks MAGS will keep beating SOX, and finds China tech contrarian-interesting.
Hartnett is 'nibbling' at peak-yield plays (GT30, small cap, REITs, HK property) while most investors wait for 6% on Treasuries. Big picture view: stay long gold, commodities and emerging markets.

tension_points.bull_case: An October hike to cap yields would signal the Fed is serious about inflation, bring term premium down and let stocks stop worrying about 6% on the 10Y.
tension_points.bear_case: If the Fed does not hike, the bond market keeps spiking since the neutral anchor line has been cut and rates rise until data or markets say stop.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rollover in US macro data or markets saying stop would mark the peak in rates; 6% on the 10Y is where bond buyers are waiting.

tension_points.bull_case: GOP Senate with Dem House ('Gridlock = Goldilocks') sends stocks up more than 5%; a GOP sweep sends them up more than 10%.
tension_points.bear_case: A Democratic sweep, which the market currently sees as most likely at 64%, would send stocks down more than 10% on higher tax and regulation and less political capital for Trump.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Texas polling as the tell: Abbott at 48% vs Hinojosa at 46%, and the Nov 3 results.

tension_points.bull_case: US hard data, global forward EPS and hyperscaler capex expectations have not rolled over, so S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 sit at record highs.
tension_points.bear_case: Biting is happening at the edges (CCC spreads at 1,200bps, Korean brokers, French OATs) and the Bull & Bear Indicator is in sell territory.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rollover in hyperscaler capex expectations or US macro data.
